_note: lockOrientation= — the universal screen-orientation attribute, and the `orientation` module's lock/unlock actions, share ONE pure core (parity/F07-orientation.md). resolve[] pins the vocabulary fold: the seven words (portrait · portraitUpsideDown · landscape · landscapeLeft · landscapeRight · all · current) expand to a MASK, which is then intersected with the app's build-time allowed set in canonical order; an unrecognized word is `unknown_orientation` and an empty intersection is `not_allowed`, both REFUSED LOUDLY rather than silently doing nothing (which is what every third-party RN library does, and why a lock that quietly no-ops is the hardest orientation bug to diagnose). `primary` is the first surviving orientation, i.e. what the device rotates TO. lifecycle[] pins the claim stack, which is the actual feature: a surface claims on appear and releases on disappear, so all five dismissal paths (button pop, edge-swipe back, modal drag-dismiss, deep-link stack replacement, backgrounded return) revert through ONE funnel. A re-claim by a live id REPLACES IN PLACE and never jumps above a surface it presented; releasing a mid-stack entry leaves the top standing; the effective lock is the last live entry, or null for the app default. The imperative unlock() removes only the `imperative` entry, so a declarative claim underneath correctly takes back over.

lifecycle.name: a screen claims on appear and reverts on disappear
nesting — a landscape screen presenting a portrait sheet, then dismissing it
the whole nest unwinding restores the app default
releasing a mid-stack surface leaves the top standing
a re-claim replaces in place and never jumps above what it presented
releasing an id that never claimed is a no-op
releasing into an empty stack is a no-op
a deep link replacing the stack resets every claim
the imperative lock is just another entry, on top
unlock removes only the imperative entry and the declarative claim resumes
unlock with no declarative claim underneath returns the app default
an idempotent repeat claim does not stack up
